name: Ilami Kurdish
confidence_why: Karimipour, Ghaderi and Alinezhad 2017 find final stress in Ilami nouns and compounds and Afshar and Ghasemi 2024 find stem-initial stress in Ilami verbs, two independent first-hand studies that agree once word class is taken into account, but they are the only two, neither is a full grammar, and the verb study rests on ten forms of a single verb.

new_statements.quote: As shown above, a disyllabic foot is regularly made of a weak (= w) and strong (=s) syllable. It is noteworthy that the main stress of the word is usually realized on the final syllable of the ultimate foot [...]. Nevertheless, there is a specific phonological context where the primary stress falls on the initial syllable of the disyllabic words. [p.198:] in all the compounds mentioned above, this is the final syllable of the last foot that takes the primary stress of the construction.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the final syllable of the word (examples mu.ˈrəʒ 'ant', kæɭ.ɭæ.ˈʃer 'rooster', kwə.t͡ʃəg.gɑ.ˈnəg); in compounds and multi-word lexicalised phrases the final syllable of the last member carries primary stress regardless of length.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Only in passing: in compounds a non-final member 'will not bear the strong stress (but it may take the secondary/tertiary one)' (p.198); metrical trees mark alternating s/w syllables but no explicit secondary-stress rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: A small set of disyllables stressed on the first syllable in neutral (non-focus) pronunciation: ˈrɐqwəɭ (a vegetable), ˈnɐqwəl 'candy', ˈnɐqət 'shut up!', ˈfɐkər 'thought', ˈʃɐkər 'thank God'; the authors analyse these as originally monosyllabic (CVCC) words with optional schwa epenthesis that does not shift stress (rɐqwl -> ˈrɐ.qwəl). They also label the system quantity-sensitive/iambic on thin evidence. Separately, Afshar & Ghasemi 2024 (abstract only) report that finite VERBS are not final-stressed (stress on the first or second syllable of the stem, affixes unstressed).
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) stress of monomorphemic nouns/adjectives and compounds in citation/neutral pronunciation ('the neutral way of articulating the words', focus forms excluded); elicited from 9 adult native speakers of Ilam city with picture/written prompts, compounds checked in PRAAT. Inflected verbs and affixal morphology are outside the paper's scope.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted source describes Ilami Kurdish, the Southern Kurdish vernacular of Ilam city (c. 200,000 speakers per the authors), i.e. the Ilami/Feyli branch of Southern Kurdish (Glottolog sout2640; no separate glottocode for Ilami). The authors group it with Kermanshahi and note it 'shares some features with Kermanshahi.. but shows some idiosyncratic characteristics'. It is not a description of Kalhori or Kermanshahi proper; the closely related Harsini/Laki-Kermanshahi variety is already catalogued separately under laki1244 (Belelli 2021, final stress with morphological conditioning), and Fattah (2000) treats all of these as Southern Kurdish.

new_statements.quote: p. 3: "it seems that in the category of verbs, unlike in Persian, the stress is not on the last syllable. Instead, the stressed syllable in Kurdish is in the initial part of the word. [...] in the verb category, stress in two-syllable words is on the first syllable. With the increase in the number of syllables in the word, which occurs by adding affixes, the second syllable is stressed. There is no stress on the affixes, and the stress is always on one of the initial syllables of the simple word." p. 18: "در مقولة نحوی فعل برخلاف زبان فارسی، تکیه روی هجای آخر قرار نمی‌گیرد و هجای تکیه‌بر در زبان کردی روی یکی از هجاهای آغازین قرار می‌گیرد." new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's fixed: final syllable record (Karimipour, Ghaderi & Alinezhad 2017, which generalises over nouns/compounds and says 'usually realized on the final syllable') by restricting its domain: in VERB forms stress is non-final, near the left edge (1st or 2nd syllable, stem-bound). Taken literally against a blanket fixed: final syllable rule this is a different placement, so the language looks category-sensitive (final in nouns and compounds; stem-initial region in verbs), much as Persian is. Evidence is thin (one verb, 7/10 forms non-significant). Live URL re-tried: connection timed out; the Internet Archive copy held by the project (web.archive.org/web/20240707054829i…
new_statements.rule_in_words: VERBS ONLY: word stress in Ilami Kurdish verb forms is not final (contrast Persian); it sits at the left edge of the simple (stem) word: first syllable in disyllabic verb forms, second syllable in longer forms built by affixation; affixes are said to be unstressed; F0 is the acoustic correlate (intensity and duration not decisive). Evidence: 10 inflected forms of one verb, ʔalesân 'wake up' (ئەڵسام 'I woke up', ئەڵسامە, دئەڵسام, ئەڵسایم, ئەڵس, نەڵس, نەڵسام, ئەڵسم, باد ئەڵسم, دێرم ئەڵسم), 5 male speakers x 3 repetitions, Praat + SPSS.
new_statements.exceptions: Only 3 of the 10 forms show a statistically significant F0 difference between syllables: present perfect ئەڵسامە -> 2nd syllable (p. 14), negative past نەڵسام -> 1st syllable (p. 17), present progressive دێرم ئەڵسم -> 2nd syllable (p. 18); for the other 7 forms (simple past, past progressive, pluperfect, imperative, prohibitive, simple present, subjunctive present) the tests are 'عدم معناداری' (non-significant), pp. 13-17. Note the internal tension: the stressed 1st syllable of نەڵسام is the negative prefix na-, which does not match the authors' 'no stress on the affixes'. The paper also notes that future tense has no grammatical marker (adverb + present form). Digits in the Persian text layer are font-garbled; page numbers were verified with extracted text per page.
new_statements.identity_note: Both works concern Ilami (Feyli) Southern Kurdish of Ilam city/province. Borjian 2017 places Feyli/'Ilami' as a Southern Kurdish dialect continuum across southwestern Kermanshahan, Ilam and Iraqi Diyala, distinct from Feyli Northern Lori; Afshar & Ghasemi's speakers are native Ilami speakers resident in Ilam from birth (p. 12-13). Karimipour et al. 2017 (existing statement) is the same Ilam-city variety.

readall_conflicts: One domain-level disagreement: the catalog record and the existing Karimipour et al. 2017 statement give final stress (right-bounded, final syllable of the last foot; final syllable of compounds), whereas Afshar & Ghasemi 2024 find for verb forms that stress is NOT final but on one of the initial syllables (1st in disyllables, 2nd in longer affixed forms). The two are reconcilable as a category split (nouns/compounds final, verbs left-edge/stem-bound), the same split Persian shows, so it is treated as a refinement rather than a contradiction; but the verb study rests on ten inflected forms of a single verb with only three forms reaching significance, and its own significant negative-past result (stress on the prefix na-) sits badly with its 'affixes unstressed' rule. Borjian 2017 is silent and conflicts with nothing.

sources.note: Dedicated stress study (9 speakers, elicitation + PRAAT): main word stress usually on the final syllable (rightmost, iambic feet, End Rule Final); a small set of disyllables (originally monosyllables with epenthetic schwa: ráqwəɭ, náqwəl, fákər..) have initial stress; compounds take primary stress on the final syllable of the last member; claims quantity-sensitivity; 'right-bounded variety'.
